Sur le boulevard Léger, dans le quartier: On Léger Boulevard in the Montréal-Nord neighbourhood, you’ll find Chamaz Barbershop. It’s a hair salon popular with residents of Montréal-Nord, as well as Rivière-des-Prairies. Its popularity is down to one man: Fedler Exilus. Fedler owns Chamaz, but above all he is a proud resident of the neighbourhood. La Converse caught up with him while he was cutting a client’s hair. So it was in the midst of teenagers, children accompanied by their big sister and older customers that Fedler finished styling his client. In the back room of Chamaz, the young owner then told us about the strong bond between his shop and his neighbourhood.
Originaire de Rivière-des-Prairies et ay: Originally from Rivière-des-Prairies and having done much of his schooling in Montréal-Nord, Fedler Exilus, a 27-year-old Haitian barber, is standing his ground, geographically at least. With his barbershop open in the place where he grew up, Fedler now embraces his desire to succeed among his own people and his community. “My father wanted me to be an engineer or a doctor, and he didn’t really believe in my barbershop project. Then, from seeing me get up every morning to go to work and seeing that I wasn’t hanging out in the streets, he ended up accepting it,” says the barber, citing his father as a source of motivation. A motivation, because his father never wanted to believe in his son’s project, hoping for another path for him.
Une raison qui a poussé Fedler à se surp: It was a reason that pushed Fedler to outdo himself, to prove his father wrong and show that he could succeed in a field he ended up loving. If his father was a source of motivation for him, he is also the reason Fedler turned, in spite of himself, toward this career: “I have five brothers, and when I was little, my father, for financial reasons, couldn’t take us to the barber regularly. So he was the one who cut our hair, and honestly, the result wasn’t very, very pretty,” he says with a smile. “So one evening, I picked up the clippers and started cutting my own hair, and it wasn’t so bad! So much so that my brothers encouraged me by trusting me with their heads, and believe me, you don’t trust someone with your head if you don’t have confidence in them.”
Au-delà de cette motivation et de sa dét: Beyond this motivation and his determination to make his father proud, Fedler doesn’t forget what his father has instilled in him: “Since we were little, our father has been telling my brothers and me to work for what we want, and to this day, he’s right.”
Pendant presque deux ans, le jeune appre: For almost two years, the young apprentice practised on his brothers, then on his friends in the neighbourhood: “I started charging $2 or $3 for my cuts. In high school, I found another clientele through my friends and the guys on my basketball team. Then, in CEGEP, where I was doing a technical program in mechanical engineering, things weren’t going well, but I still ended up in a barbershop. From cutting my brothers’ and friends’ hair, I got a taste for it and developed my passion,” says Fedler, proud of his journey.
Sa conversion professionnelle a fait naî: His career change gave rise to unshakeable motivation and ambition: “You can start from nothing and still succeed. When I opened my shop, I had nothing, almost no savings, and yet, with my motivation, I always got up in the morning to come to work. I’m no smarter than anyone else,” Fedler says, explaining what forged his character. “Even when going through tough times, I always told myself there was an emergency exit, a tunnel you take where you eventually see the light; you just have to really want it. There’s nothing wrong with working harder than others to get what you want.” It is a destiny and a set of circumstances he is very grateful for today and wants to share and pass on: “Doing what I love from a very young age, which is cutting hair, always kept me from hanging out outside and getting into trouble. I bet everything on this shop, putting my whole soul into it.”
Si le salon de Fedler a vu le jour, c’es: Fedler’s shop came to be in part thanks to the encouragement of his family and friends in the neighbourhood. “In the neighbourhood, when one of us has a project, everybody tries to push them so that it can stay in the neighbourhood as a way of giving back to the community. That’s why I decided to keep this shop in Montréal-Nord,” says the young man.
L’enfant la Rivière-des-Prairies met en: The Rivière-des-Prairies kid highlights his brothers’ contribution and the natural bond between the neighbourhoods. It’s a bond Fedler wants to bring into his professional life: “My brothers have always been there, even for the renovations of my shop or to support my project, and that means a lot to me. Whether in my family or with my friends, we’ve always been tight and happy despite everything, and that’s what I want to bring to my work and to this neighbourhood.”
Avec le Chamaz Barbershop, Fedler veut b: With Chamaz Barbershop, Fedler wants to break stereotypes, even though he doesn’t deny certain realities of working-class neighbourhoods. “Whether in Rivière-des-Prairies or Montréal-Nord, we live in disadvantaged neighbourhoods where there is still violence, but with my shop, I’m trying to show that that’s not the only side of us,” he says, before pointing to his shop’s greatest strength: “I cut because I love it and I love the atmosphere it creates. An atmosphere you’ve always known, really, cutting the hair of the young people or even the families in your neighbourhood. My shop truly brings everyone together. People from all communities, all neighbourhoods and all ages – and it’s that mix that creates the atmosphere at Chamaz and, in a way, brings life and colour back to the residents of Montréal-Nord.”
<strong>Fedler et les jeunes, une relati: Fedler and the youth, a father-son relationship
« Les jeunes d’ici disent que je suis co: “The young people here say I’m like a dad to them and that I have a lot of kids,” Fedler says. Over the years, the man who has become a father figure has seen many young people come through his shop and has cut the hair of a great many of them. “When you cut a client’s hair, whether they’re young or not, you share a moment with them. Some proudly tell me about the trouble they get into, so I always try to talk to them and advise them, to help them grasp all the possibilities open to them. I get some of them to practise cutting hair, and if it’s not for them, they will still have tried and will keep that experience.”
En accord avec certains établissements s: In agreement with certain high schools, the owner of Chamaz often hosts student interns. He teaches them the barber’s trade, but in a playful way, having fun. He has noticed that some get a taste for it, to the point of launching into hairstyling. Fedler has even hired two of them, who now work with him. “I’m proud of that, because it’s like I’m passing on a part of myself and of my passion so they can benefit from it and succeed. Find a passion and commit to it fully, find a reason to get up in the morning, find something to keep yourself busy and not hang around outside getting into trouble” – that is the advice of this Montréal-Nord “dad.”
Quand on lui demande si l’argent est sou: When asked whether money is often the cause of the trouble, Fedler answers categorically: “You can do something other than sell drugs or whatever, you can make money legally and love it, and not only in medicine or engineering either. You can open your own business and love it, whether it’s in hairstyling, nails or whatever.”
Au fil de son parcours, grâce à sa déter: Over the course of his journey, thanks to his determination, Fedler Exilus, supported by those around him, has succeeded without ever uprooting himself. Beyond his success, he remains involved in his neighbourhood’s community through his shop, which he puts at everyone’s service. His story could not end any other way than with his own words: “You can come from a disadvantaged neighbourhood, start from zero, have nobody believing in you and, despite it all, end up standing out from the crowd and getting where you want to be. Of course that will inspire everyone, the whole community, young and old alike.”
